clue.text: Wife has to leave reversible grass skirts in garbage

indicators.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge, so the drug word wraps the other letters

parts.note: grass is slang for cannabis, and hash (hashish) is another name for it

indicators.note: something reversible can be turned the other way, so this pair is read backwards
one piece has the other beside it, joining them in order

parts.note: to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A tangle of domestic odds: a wife departing, a two-way grass skirt, and talk of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass skirts' looks like a hula outfit, but 'grass' is a drug and 'skirts' means surrounds; 'reversible' gives OGW.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive words for worthless nonsense, rubbish talk or ideas: a straight synonym.

clue.text: Play, collection of books and magazine

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a collection of books of the Bible
Hello! is a British celebrity magazine

explanation.surface: A drama, a library and a periodical, as if in a bookshop.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's tragedy, a stage work.

clue.text: Crazy king in Texas city

indicators.note: in places the chess abbreviation inside the town's name

parts.note: Waco is a city in Texas
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A mad monarch holed up in Texas.
explanation.definitionFit: Wacko is slang for eccentric or mad, a synonym of crazy.

clue.text: Flash on you, blue collars for dog

indicators.note: a collar circles a neck, so the sad word goes round the pair

parts.note: blue means low in spirits, sad

indicators.note: on joins the moment and the old word for you in order

parts.note: a flash, like a mo, is a moment
ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Showing off your blue collars to a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Samoyed is a fluffy white Siberian breed of working dog.

clue.text: Attack shabby cloth with plain clothing

indicators.note: clothing something covers it, so the plain word goes round the cloth

parts.note: plain, unadorned, means bare
a rag is a scrap of worn, shabby cloth

explanation.surface: An assault on a ragged fabric in a simple outfit, as if fashion were a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy, concentrated bombardment, a kind of military attack.

clue.text: Gear towards exhaust

parts.note: at means towards, as in throwing at
to tire is to exhaust

explanation.surface: Car parts and the exhaust, a garage conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear means clothes, kit, the same as attire: a synonym.

clue.text: Rounding Cape at sea, more ready to eat delicate stuff?

indicators.note: rounding means going around, so the riper word surrounds the rearranged letters

parts.note: riper means more ready to be eaten

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sailors rounding a cape, keen to eat delicacies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rounding Cape' looks nautical, but 'at sea' is the anagram signal; the question mark flags a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rice paper is a thin, delicate edible sheet, delicate stuff indeed.

clue.text: Outspoken visitor, it's supposed

indicators.note: outspoken means spoken out, so the visitor word is said aloud

parts.note: a guest is a visitor

explanation.surface: A blunt guest, it's assumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Guessed and supposed both mean believed without proof: synonyms.

clue.text: Star protecting a chum, being devious killer

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping around, so the star surrounds the rest

parts.note: the Sun is a star

indicators.note: devious means winding, crooked, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity guards a friend who is a sly killer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' looks like a link verb but is part of the fodder for 'devious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A submachine gun is a light automatic weapon, a killing tool.

clue.text: Smart young thing dropping back

indicators.note: the young creature's word loses its back, meaning its final letter

parts.note: a chick is a young bird, a young thing

explanation.surface: A stylish youngster falls behind the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic describes stylish elegance, as smart does of dress: a synonym.

clue.text: Swimming costume has trimmed features

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters are swirling about and rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimsuit that sports neat trims, like a catalogue description of beachwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed features' looks like tailoring on the costume, but means neatly clipped facial hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-lip hair kept trimmed is a feature of the face, so these are trimmed features.

clue.text: Dark gymslips covering the ladies, perhaps?

indicators.note: covering something puts it inside, so the rearranged letters surround the toilet

parts.note: read as gym plus slips: the three letters of gym slip out of order, rearranged within the one word
the Ladies is one example of a loo, a public toilet

explanation.surface: Schoolgirls' gymslips hiding the women's toilets, a gloomy little scene.
explanation.walkthrough: A gymslip is a British schoolgirl's pinafore; the word must be split, with 'slips' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloomy and dark both describe a place with little light: synonyms.

clue.text: Lily a soak, one on reflection beyond ruin

indicators.note: beyond means coming after, so this group follows the word for ruin

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so this group is read backwards

parts.note: a sop is a piece of bread soaked in liquid, so sop serves for soak
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drunk, on reflection, is past saving: the lily is decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' is a noun for a drunkard in the surface but a verb clue for sop; 'beyond' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: The mariposa lily is a North American flowering plant, so lily names the kind.

clue.text: Rollers destroying deep rock, one coming in

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so the numeral goes inside the rearranged letters
destroying the two words breaks them up so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Rollers, waves pounding deep rock, with one breaking through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rollers' suggests waves, but means things that are rolled; 'destroying' gives POKERDCE before the I enters.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker dice are dice marked with card values, which players roll, so they are rollers.

clue.text: Cease to be a postman packaging gold evening dresses

indicators.note: dresses means clothes, so the evening word covers the rest

parts.note: eve is an old word for evening

indicators.note: packaging wraps, so the postman wraps the gold

parts.note: Postman Pat is a British children's TV postman
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A postman bundling gold evening dresses, then vanishing.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat is a British children's TV character; 'evening dresses' looks like gowns but 'dresses' means covers.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to vanish, to cease to exist: a figurative sense.

clue.text: Composition written by snooker player starts: "I'm a famous potter"

indicators.note: written by puts the poem after the pair of first letters
the starts of the two words are their first letters

parts.note: an ode is a lyrical poetic composition

explanation.surface: A snooker player opens his poem by boasting of his skill potting balls.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker, potting is sinking balls; the famous potter here is Josiah Spode, the English pottery maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Josiah Spode founded the English ceramics firm, so the name speaks as a celebrated maker of china.

clue.text: Fancy opening in extremely short trousers

indicators.note: to trouser is to pocket, so the measure of spirits holds the letter

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, a dram

indicators.note: the opening in the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A fashion fantasy about very brief trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short trousers' looks like a garment, but 'short' is a dram and 'trousers' means pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to imagine it, and a dream is an imagined fancy: synonyms.

clue.text: Whale getting thinner finally, or the same topless?

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word
topless removes the top, the first letter

parts.note: equal means the same

explanation.surface: A whale slimming down, or still the same without a top.
explanation.definitionFit: The rorqual is a type of baleen whale, such as the blue whale.

clue.text: Past master in sari and hot pants

indicators.note: pants, as British slang for rubbish, signals that these letters are a mess to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An expert dressed in a sari and hot pants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Past master' usually means an expert; here it is one who masters the past. 'pants' (British slang for bad) is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A historian studies past events, so is literally a master of the past.

clue.text: By the sound of it, credit secured

indicators.note: by the sound of it means as heard, so the credit word is said aloud

parts.note: trust is credit, belief

explanation.surface: Credit sounds secured, a banker's assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussed means tied up firmly, so secured: synonyms.

clue.text: Disturbed, alas, with our awakening

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Alas, our sleep is disturbed by an awakening.
explanation.definitionFit: Arousal is the act of waking or stirring up, an awakening: synonym.

clue.text: Waste of some stock, wide and soft jacket pockets

indicators.note: pockets means puts inside, so the jacket holds the pair

parts.note: a coat is an outer jacket
W is the cricket abbreviation for wide
P is piano, the musical instruction to play softly

explanation.surface: Livestock waste and a soft wide jacket with pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' is livestock; a wide is a cricket extra, W.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock includes cattle, and dung from a cow is their waste.

clue.text: Oil broken-down scooter with last of lube

indicators.note: a broken-down machine is in pieces, so its letters are rearranged
the last of the word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A broken-down scooter that needs oil and the last of the lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: Creosote is an oily preservative distilled from tar, so is a kind of oil.

clue.text: Small wedding veils in harmony

indicators.note: veils cover and hide, so the marriage word wraps the letter

parts.note: a wedding is a union of two people
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A modest wedding with veils, everyone in harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison is singing or acting together as one, agreement in harmony: a synonym.

clue.text: Country is now delivering immensely accomplished leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A nation now producing immensely talented leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation in South Asia, a country.

clue.text: Sweet things happy to eat fish in shanty towns

indicators.note: in places the happy word with its fish inside the word for poor districts

parts.note: shanty towns are slums, makeshift poor settlements

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so the happy word swallows the fish

parts.note: up means cheerful, happy
a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Cheerful people feasting on fish among the shacks of a shanty town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'happy' is a person in the surface but simply gives a word meaning cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugarplums are small round sweets, so they are sweet things.

clue.text: Style in T-shirt and Y-fronts, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: the short horizontal mark joining T to shirt and Y to fronts is a punctuation stroke

explanation.surface: Can a man in underwear and a tee have style?
explanation.walkthrough: Y-fronts are British men's briefs with an inverted-Y front opening.
explanation.definitionFit: Style as panache, and the punctuation line printed within both garment names.

clue.text: Wary about British premier, a Canadian province

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wary word goes round the letter

parts.note: alert means watchful, wary

indicators.note: premier means first, so the word gives its first letter

explanation.surface: A cautious note about a British prime minister and a Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts B, the first letter of British, inside ALERT, and 'a' adds the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberta is one of Canada's western provinces, with Edmonton its capital.

clue.text: I waste time cuddling sweetheart in the best possible way

indicators.note: cuddling something holds it close, so the time-wasting word wraps the letter

parts.note: to dally is to dawdle, waste time
the heart of sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Someone dawdles while cuddling their sweetheart, which is perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideally means in a perfect manner, under the best circumstances: an adverb synonym.
